items.headline: Cardinals Remain Beckless, Josh Johnson The Sequel, And Friday Before The Commanders
items.summary: Cardinals Remain Beckless, Josh Johnson The Sequel, And Friday Before The Commanders
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: Presented by Cardinals Remain Beckless, Josh Johnson The Sequel, And Friday Before The Commanders Nov 27, 2026 at 02:36 PM Darren Urban/Word From The Birds azcardinals.com Copied! The Cardinals basically didn't have Carson Beck for a couple of weeks earlier this season because of his back spasms, a moment in time that was mostly invisible because he was the third quarterback. So the news that he was going to miss a second straight start this week with those same kind of back issues was not a surprise to coach Mike LaFleur. Beck could return next week. If he does, and stays healthy, that's a six-game sample size of evaluation. Not ideal. But not crippling. "The most important is Sunday, no doubt," LaFleur said Friday after ruling Beck out. "But we get to see things in practice that (media) obviously don't get to see, that the people don't get to see. I know where we stand with it right now. We want to get them out there as much as we can on those Sundays, obviously. But those are not the cards we were dealt." So it's Week 2 of the Josh Johnson experience. And Johnson faces the team for whom he started a game for in the 2025 season finale in Washington. The Commanders OC is former Cardinals QB David Blough, who was Johnson's assistant QB coach in Washington last year. Johnson said the Commanders' defense is dramatically different than the time he spent there. But with finally a full week of practice as a starter, Johnson said there is a "different kind of calm" to the Cardinals' offensive situation. "I've been able to see what guys can do in real time, as opposed to seeing a rep for the first time on Sunday," Johnson said.

items.headline: Teryl Austin Hopes Simplicity, Freedom Helps Cardinals Defense Improve
items.summary: Interim defensive coordinator will call plays from sideline
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: Teryl Austin Hopes Simplicity, Freedom Helps Cardinals Defense Improve Interim defensive coordinator will call plays from sideline Nov 26, 2026 at 01:23 PM Darren Urban azcardinals.com Copied! Jeremy Chen/Arizona Cardinals Interim defensive coordinator Teryl Austin (right) chats with safety Budda Baker, taking a rest day, before Wednesday's practice. Teryl Austin had been on the other end of an in-season defensive coordinator change before, when he was with the Bengals in 2018. It isn't an ideal situation for any team. But as Austin took over this week as interim defensive coordinator of the Cardinals after Nick Rallis was fired by head coach Mike LaFleur on Monday, the message with six games left in the season is simply to "push on." "We have to try and improve," Austin said Thanksgiving morning, "because obviously we need to." Austin, who had been a senior defensive assistant this season working behind to scenes to aid Rallis and give advice where he could to both sides of the ball, has been a coordinator three previous times: with the Lions, the aforementioned Bengals, and most recently the last four seasons with the Steelers under then head-coach Mike Tomlin. LaFleur said Austin will be considered for the permanent DC role in 2027. But first comes the balance of 2026. The Cardinals have given up at least 30 points in eight of their 11 games, are 31 st in points allowed, and 28 th in takeaways. Wholesale changes are impossible at this point in the season, Austin said. Some tweaks will happen, but it is Austin trying to learn a new verbiage in order to call plays. He will work on the sidelines and not the press box, emphasizing the need for in-game interaction with the players as they go through this change on the fly.

items.body: After Defensive Coordinator Change, Players Adjust On The Fly Nick Rallis moves on as Teryl Austin tweaks current system Nov 25, 2026 at 03:56 PM Darren Urban azcardinals.com Copied! Caitlyn Epes Kerl/Arizona Cardinals Linebacker Mack Wilson Sr. (1) and the rest of the Cardinals defense is learning the new style of interim defensive coordinator Teryl Austin. When was drafted, Darius Robinson got a helmet and had his fellow draftees sign it, as well as the coaches. He was thinking of that helmet on Wednesday, talking about the change at defensive coordinator from Nick Rallis to Teryl Austin, thinking of the names scribbled on the gear. Rallis. Former head coach Jonathan Gannon. Fellow first-round pick Marvin Harrison Jr. "I got something with all of us," Robinson said with a smile. "The relationships, and realizing what every guy meant to me personally, because you never know how things will spin. "I'm just putting my best foot forward so I can stay here as long as possible." With Austin taking over this week and with six games left to play, defensive players said there are minor tweaks and some new plays incoming with the change from Rallis. But ultimately, it was a this-stuff-happens approach in a league that needs to see results. New DC Teryl Austin pic.twitter.com/4jXKD3INVO — Darren Urban (@Cardschatter) November 25, 2026 "You don't want to see anyone get fired, but we know the nature of this business," linebacker Mack Wilson Sr. said. "Coach Rallis poured a lot into us, and I developed a great relationship with him. It was somebody who really gave me my first opportunity, trusted in me. "We have to take it for what it is. You just have to be better as a defense, as a team.

Jeremy Chen/Arizona Cardinals Rookie Carson Beck (right) has a moment with fellow QB Josh Johnson during a practice last week. For now, Carson Beck is still sidelined. Coach Mike LaFleur said the rookie quarterback was not practicing on Wednesday as he continues to deal with back spasms. "That's typical from the last time. Every day he got better." Beck dealt with back spasms last month, although as third QB at the time, the impact was minimal. "There is always going to be a concern, so you are trying to find ways to strengthen it, treat it, prehab to try and limit this, particularlyÂ this year," LaFleur said. "Then in the offseason you really attack it to prevent this, if you can." LaFleur said he wasn't thinking past this week yet with Beck. The Cardinals are not contemplating IR. Beck was to throw some on Wednesday on the side. Johnson completed 18 of 31 passes in Kansas City last weekend for 155 yards and a touchdown. He did not turn the ball over although the Cardinals lost, 34-7. "This isn't something that you necessarily feel good about," Johnson said after the game. "I am grateful for the opportunity.

items.summary: Topics include DC move, bye weeks, and Beck spasms

items.body: You've Got Mail: Change Has Been In The Air Topics include DC move, bye weeks, and Beck spasms Nov 24, 2026 at 12:23 PM Darren Urban azcardinals.com Copied! A new defensive coordinator . Uncertainty at quarterback . A stable mailbag.Â Don't forget to send a question for a future mailbag with at least a first name and last initial . From John F : "Darren, I have mixed emotions about Rallis. I hate seeing that happen to people. But I think they needed to change him out. But I don't know if it's really going to make a difference. Why are my emotions all over the place?" Frankly John, I cannot speak for you or your emotions. Coaching changes in-season are what they are. You're not going to fundamentally change a team or part of a team by moving out one coach, not after the months spent installing what is already installed. This isn't like adding a pitcher at the trade deadline. I will agree with Mike LaFleur in that some kind of dramatic change was needed, to get that jolt. I definitely do not lay this all on Rallis; this defense was solid enough for a good enough chunk of his tenure that you can't convince me he can't do it. But it got sideways this season, and this league is what it is when it comes to results. From Steve from logistics : "How is the bye week determined? Seems the last few years, the Cards have had one of the last bye weeks each time. Not saying an earlier one would do any good, but curious." Gosh Steve, I will open with the thought that ... man, the Cardinals (and myself, for that matter, because yes, I think about me) really could use a bye week, say, right now. Or two weeks ago. Just not Dec. 13. But here we are. Here are the bye weeks for the Cardinals since 2020: Week 8, Week 12, Week 13, Week 14, Week 11, Week 8, Week 14.

items.body: Cardinals Move On From Nick Rallis, Make Teryl Austin Defensive Coordinator Change comes with 6 games left in 2026 season Published: Nov 23, 2026 at 03:58 PM Updated: Nov 23, 2026 at 05:35 PM Darren Urban azcardinals.com Copied! Jeremy Chen/Arizona Cardinals Teryl Austin (left) and coach Mike LaFleur speak at a minicamp practice this offseason. Mike LaFleur said recently that the Cardinals' season was now in evaluation mode. After Sunday's 34-7 road loss to the Chiefs, the head coach acted on some of the evaluation, firing defensive coordinator Nick Rallis on Monday. Senior defensive assistant Teryl Austin, who has served as a defensive coordinator with three other NFL teams, will move into an interim defensive coordinator role for the balance of the season, LaFleur said.Â He emphasized it was his decision. "I just felt in my heart this morning we needed a change," LaFleur said. "A fresh voice." LaFleur called Rallis an "utmost professional" in telling him about the move. He added that Rallis told him to say how much he was going to miss the locker room, organization, city and fanbase. Rallis had been a holdover from Jonathan Gannon's staff, hired in 2023, and kept by LaFleur when LaFleur was hired in January. LaFleur acknowledged his late hire took away some options to hire as DC, but keeping Rallis made sense after having gone against Rallis often with the Rams. Unlike the offense, the defense has been relatively healthy this season, save for a year-ending neck injury to top cornerback Will Johnson. The Cardinals have allowed at least 30 points in eight of 11 games this season and are 31st in the NFL in points allowed at 29.4. "It has not been good enough collectively," LaFleur said. "All phases. As a team.

items.summary: Rookie wide receiver has four receptions against Chiefs
items.impact: +2 boosts Harrison Wallace III's usage — full go or an expanded role.
items.body: Presented by Harrison Wallace III Sees More Snaps And Chance To Be Showcased Rookie wide receiver has four receptions against Chiefs Nov 23, 2026 at 11:13 AM Darren Urban/Word From The Birds azcardinals.com Copied! Where the Cardinals moved on from one Harrison, another Harrison emerges. What the long-term evaluation of undrafted rookie wide receiver Harrison Wallace III will be is TBD, but he is one of the options the Cardinals now have at the position after all the injuries and the trade of Marvin Harrison Jr. And while Sunday's game was not a good result for the Cardinals, this is where you start to look for pockets of success. Wallace, who played 36 snaps (after playing a total of seven the previous two games) and made an excellent 25-yard reception among his four catches for a team-best 57 yards, formed a pocket against the Chiefs. "There will be some opportunities for otherÂ guys to show that they are going to be a part of the solution moving forward," coach Mike LaFleur said. "He is definitely a guy thatÂ (the moment) is not too big for him. There is certainly a long way to go in terms of details and stuff,Â but I think his transitions have been nice. ... I am looking forward to him continuing. He has been a bright spot for us. I am looking forward to continuing to showcase him." Wallace said the week of prep was "a little crazy," given that the team had to pivot from QB Carson Beck to QB Josh Johnson late in the week. Wallace already knew he was part of the plan, seeing how the depth chart was working out beginning Wednesday. "I just want to take advantage of my opportunities," Wallace said, saying he was just "living in the moment." "Honestly, it's just being prepared," he said.

items.summary: Mahomes makes life difficult in 34-7 defeat
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: As Josh Johnson Takes Turn In Quarterback Shuffle, Cardinals Fall To Chiefs Mahomes makes life difficult in 34-7 defeat Nov 22, 2026 at 03:22 PM Darren Urban azcardinals.com Copied! Caitlyn Epes Kerl/Arizona Cardinals Defensive lineman Walter Nolen III hauls down Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes for a sack during the Cardinals' loss Sunday in Kansas City. THE STORY: KANSAS CITY, Mo. â After Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur gathered the team postgame for what he called the "realist" conversation they have had. "I like to think we keep it real with each other," LaFleur said. "It's been a tough stretch. Four different quarterbacks in four different weeks, which doesn't happen too often in this league. It's not an excuse, it's just reality. (But) I know we can still be better than that regardless of the situation. "It's been one hell of a stretch for us." The chilly, windy day at Arrowhead Stadium ended in a 34-7 loss, with Josh Johnson the aforementioned fourth quarterback starter in as many weeks for the Cardinals (3-8). Johnson, he of the 82 career NFL transactions, did what he could on short notice. Rookie Carson Beck, the guy who was supposed to start, suffered a reoccurrence of back spasms late in Thursday's practice. That meant that Johnson, who had signed just 12 days prior, got one practice with the starters. "It's challenging, not only on myself but on the guys," Johnson acknowledged afterward. "But you can't dwell on that." It not surprisingly showed against the Chiefs (8-2), who are trying to make their way back to the Super Bowl. Johnson didn't turn the ball over, completing 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown.

items.body: Josh Johnson Start Confirmed After Carson Beck Downgraded Rookie quarterback will be inactive with back spasms Published: Nov 21, 2026 at 12:21 PM Updated: Nov 21, 2026 at 02:00 PM Darren Urban azcardinals.com Copied! Jeremy Chen/Arizona Cardinals QB Josh Johnson throws a pass during a recent practice KANSAS CITY, Mo. - The Cardinals made it official on Saturday:Â Josh Johnson will start at quarterback on Sunday against the Chiefs because Carson Beck will not play. Beck was officially downgraded to out by the team because of his back issues, not a shock after coach Mike LaFleur said Friday the team was proceeding on the idea Johnson would start. Rookie Joey Aguilar will be the backup. Both players just signed last week. "There is no next step to the playbook, this is going back to the starting table of contents, and that's OK," LaFleur said. "For a three-and-a-half-hour window, it's my job to to figure out as you know whatever we can to you know get the ball moving forward." Johnson will be the fourth different starting quarterback for the Cardinals in four weeks. Jacoby Brissett started in Dallas, Gardner Minshew started in Seattle, and Beck started last week at home against the Rams. It will be Johnson's 12th career start and 51st NFL appearance since originally joining the league in 2009. ZAY JONES ELEVATED The Cardinals elevated wide receiver Zay Jones from the practice squad for a second straight week, the only elevation for the game.

items.summary: Needing More Trey McBride, Hello Josh Johnson, And Friday Before The Chiefs
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: Presented by Needing More Trey McBride, Hello Josh Johnson, And Friday Before The Chiefs Nov 20, 2026 at 02:10 PM Darren Urban/Word From The Birds azcardinals.com Copied! Trey McBride's birthday is on Sunday. He'll turn 27, and the All-Pro tight end will have a game to play. It doesn't mean he won't have friends over. His buddy Travis Kelce will be there in Kansas City, a guy who McBride called "a great friend" and with whom McBride has spent time with at Tight End University as well as multiple golf outings. Oh, and a guy McBride emphasizes "is one of the greatest tight ends of all time." But birthdays are also about gifts. What the Cardinals can give McBride is ways to get targets, within an offense that by now allows defenses to focus â hard â on making sure McBride doesn't receive them. McBride's streak of games with seven catches came to an end at 11 last week, lost in the reality of a new and rookie quarterback and a mere 12 offensive plays in the second half. With the top of the wide receiving room decimated with injuries, defenses have even more reasons to focus on shutting down McBride. "It's a tough game, and however they decide to cover us, I just can run my route to win and the ball will find me when it does," McBride said. "If I have two guys covering me, it means these other guys will be open. That excites me as much as me catching the ball. I just need to do my job." McBride will likely have to do that with a fourth different QB in as many games, with the knowledge rookie Carson Beck will probably be out with back spasms and Josh Johnson â who was just signed last week â will be throwing the passes . But how do the Cardinals spring McBride loose if he's all opponents -- or in the case Sunday, the Chiefs -- are thinking about?

items.headline: The blueprint is there: What the Falcons can learn from the 49ers' dismantling of the Vikings top defense
items.summary: Brock Purdy showed the way. Can Michael Penix Jr. find similar success?
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: The blueprint is there: What the Falcons can learn from the 49ers' dismantling of the Vikings top defense Brock Purdy showed the way. Can Michael Penix Jr. find similar success? Nov 25, 2026 at 03:44 PM Tori McElhaney Senior Reporter Copied! FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. â There isn't a team in the league that blitzes more than the Minnesota Vikings. There isn't a team that generates more pressure, either. Because of that, there's an argument to be made that Minnesota has the best defense in the league. That said, the Vikings aren't without weaknesses. There are areas of their defense that can be exploited, and the San Francisco 49ers just provided a blueprint for how to do it. Related Links Where to watch Atlanta Falcons vs. Minnesota Vikings Atlanta Falcons Week 12 depth chart vs. Minnesota Vikings Week 12 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Falcons return from bye, Lions contending It starts with quick decisions and easy outlets for a quarterback to take advantage of. Brock Purdy has been very good against the blitz all season. That wasn't the surprise. What was surprising was how consistently he dismantled the league's most aggressive blitzing unit. According to Next Gen Stats, Purdy completed 16 of 18 passes against the Vikings' blitz. Those completions resulted in 195 yards and two touchdowns. His 88.9% completion rate was the highest recorded against a Brian Flores-coached defense since Lamar Jackson accomplished the same feat in Week 1 of the 2019 season. What's more, Purdy was pressured on 10 of his 19 dropbacks against the blitz. He completed eight of nine passes on those pressured dropbacks, totaling 100 yards. And he did it by getting the ball out quickly. Purdy completed 12 of 13 quick passes for 161 yards and two touchdowns.

Nov 23, 2026 at 11:58 AM Tori McElhaney Senior Reporter Copied! FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. â The Atlanta Falcons have released linebacker Christian Harris. In a corresponding move, the team has signed safety Jammie Robinson to the active roster. Harris initially signed with the Falcons at the start of the new league year in March. He saw action in seven games for Atlanta, mainly on special teams where he took 79 snaps across those games. Harris spent his first four seasons in the league with the Houston Texans, who drafted him in the third round of the 2022 NFL Draft. Over the four years of his rookie deal, Harris started 27 games and accumulated four sacks and 206 total tackles (14 for a loss). He hit the quarterback seven times, forced two fumbles and had one interception. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been maneuvering Robinson across the active roster and practice squad for much of the season. He's been signed to the active roster, the practice squad and he's been used as a standard practice squad elevation for game days a couple times this season. He's seen action in four games this year, mainly 93 snaps on special teams. To backfill Robinson's spot on the practice squad, the Falcons have signed cornerback Terell Smith. Smith was a fifth-round selection by the Chicago Bears in 2023. He has spent the 2026 season to this point on the Commanders and Steelers practice squads. Smith is originally from Snellville, Georgia, and he attended South Gwinnett High School. items.body: Devontez Walker Named AFC Special Teams Player of the Week Nov 25, 2026 at 12:00 PM Quentin Corpuel Editorial Associate Copied! Devontez Walker's fireworks on special teams against the Carolina Panthers in Week 11 earned him AFC Special Teams Player of the Week. In his first game as a kickoff returner, Walker took a kickoff 86 yards for a touchdown in the second quarter. THE TARHEEL TEZ BACK IN CAROLINA WITH THE KICK RETURN TUDDY!!! TUNE IN ON FOX! pic.twitter.com/WdrKLHgEpM — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) November 22, 2026 It was Baltimore's first kickoff return touchdown since September 2022. It was also just the second kickoff return touchdown in the NFL this season â the other came from Las Vegas Raiders running back Dylan Laube in Week 8. The electric moment was fitting for Walker, who grew up in Charlotte, N.C., and attended North Carolina Central University as well as the University of North Carolina. Walker also had a 34-yard reception on his lone target of the afternoon. Head Coach Jesse Minter said the performance could lead to more playing time for the third-year wideout. "When you get an opportunity and you take advantage of it, there's definitely a path for more of that," Minter said on Monday. Minter also said that Walker could "potentially" be an option as a punt returner. Wide receiver LaJohntay Wester was waived on Tuesday after muffing two punts against the Panthers, one of which led to a Carolina touchdown. Walker is the second Raven to win AFC Special Teams Player of the Week this season. Ravens kicker Tyler Loop earned the honor after kicking a walk-off 56-yard field goal against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 3. ð Get better search results for Ravens content by adding BaltimoreRavens.com to yourÂ Google Source Preferences .

items.body: Presented by Late for Work: Mark Andrews Listed Among Players With Most at Stake Over Rest of Season Nov 24, 2026 at 09:38 AM Kevin Eck Writer Copied! Shawn Hubbard/Baltimore Ravens Photos TE Mark Andrews Tight end Mark Andrews' resume is undeniable. A staple of the Ravens for nearly a decade, the three-time Pro Bowler is the franchise's all-time leader in receptions, receiving yards, and touchdowns. He's been two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson's security blanket ever since they were drafted by the Ravens in 2018. While Andrews is still a key contributor, his production has dipped in recent years and he'll be 32 at the start of next season. ESPNâs Bill Barnwell included Andrews, who signed a three-year extension reportedly worth $39 million last year, on his list of players with the most to gain or lose over the remainder of the 2026 season. "Andrews is due $9.1 million in 2027, $5 million of which is already guaranteed," Barnwell wrote. "The Ravens signed that deal with the expectation that Andrews would be on the roster next year, and while he could credibly be the TE2 while making $9 million, I'm not sure they can run things back with this version of his game as the primary receiving tight end in the lineup. Andrews has been an important receiver in this offense for nearly a decade, but he'll need to show signs of a turnaround for the Ravens to keep giving him valuable snaps in the slot or as a focal point of the passing attack next season." Andrews showed that he can still be a difference-maker against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 10 when he led the Ravens in receptions (eight on eight targets) and receiving yards (82). It was revealed that Andrews had been playing with a broken hand since the Ravens' Week 3 contest in Brazil.

Tampa Ravens cornerback T.J. Tampa Jr. has waited three years for his opportunity, and he delivered on it Sunday against the Carolina Panthers. With Marlon Humphrey deactivated, Tampa played 40 defensive snaps, the second-most of his career (the other was last year's game against the Houston Texans when the Ravens' defense was riddled with injuries). While the Ravens lost, 35-33, to the Panthers, Tampa earned the defense's highest Pro Football Focus (PFF) grade with a 90.5 on 40 defensive snaps. Tampa had a stellar series in the third quarter when he broke up a slant intended for Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker in the end zone. Two plays later, Tampa undercut a Bryce Young pass to Tetairoa McMillian in the back of the end zone and made a diving interception. Big time series by TJ Tampa in Q3. Gets the pbu on 1st down then comes back with an INT on 3rd down. Check out the technique on the pick. Eyes on the receiver until heâs back in phase then he finds the ball. pic.twitter.com/uNnlwmrzW2 — MC (@abukari) November 23, 2026 It was the first interception by a Ravens cornerback this season and the second of Tampa's three-year career. "He's a physical player and tackles well," Head Coach Jesse Minter said on Monday. "I thought he held up his own and did some good things. items.headline: Top 3 things we learned from Bills vs. Chiefs
items.summary: How Joe Brady managed the clock, defensive passes a big test and Josh Allen addresses his performance.

items.body: Top 3 Things We Learned Top 3 things we learned from Bills vs. Chiefs | Thanksgiving Game Nov 27, 2026 at 12:01 PM Alec White Content Manager Copied! Bjorn Franke/Buffalo Bills Buffalo Bills vs Kansas City Chiefs, Regular Season, November 26, 2026 at Highmark Stadium. In yet another instant-classic finish between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs, the Bills won 13-10 on a field goal from Tyler Bass on the final play of regulation. Here's what we learned from the win. 1 â How the Bills managed the final 30 seconds Another thrilling chapter was added to the Bills-Chiefs rivalry Thursday night as Buffalo won on a 57-yard field goal from Tyler Bass as time expired, propelling Buffalo to their first 10-1 start since 1991. A full 60-minute ordeal of rain, wind and near-freezing temperatures provided a stage for two of the NFL's best teams to cap off Thanksgiving night. "That was one of the grossest weather games I think I've ever played," quarterback Josh Allen said. "I've played in cold games, I've played in rain games. Cold, rain games are tough. So that was again, but everyone's got to play in it, myself included. The other team's got to play in it." Tied at 10-10 with under a minute remaining, the Bills had the ball just outside of field goal range in Kansas City territory on a 3rd and 9 play. But Allen was unable to shake free of a blitz, eventually getting taken down for a sack on the Buffalo side of midfield. Rookie punter Tommy Doman Jr., who had twice earlier pinned the Chiefs inside their own 10-yard line, got off another impressive punt that was fielded by Chiefs WR Josh Downs at the 7-yard line and returned to the 11 with 26 seconds left in regulation. The Bills had all three timeouts still in their pocket.

items.body: Game Recap Presented by Bills 13, Chiefs 10 | Final Score, recap + highlights Nov 27, 2026 at 12:08 AM Mike Maynard Seasonal Writing Associate Copied! Emilee Fails/Buffalo Bills Buffalo Bills vs Kansas City Chiefs, Regular Season, November 26, 2026 at Highmark Stadium. Location: Highmark Stadium Final score: Bills 13, Chiefs 10 Records: Bills (10-1), Chiefs (8-3) Next opponent: Bills at Patriots Sunday, Dec. 6 at 4:25 p.m. EST Buffalo walked off Kansas City, winning 13-10 as time expired in the organization's first-ever home Thanksgiving game on Thursday night. It wasn't the prettiest of games for either side, but the Bills came through to build on their now seven-game winning streak. Buffalo is now 10-1 for the first time since the 1991 season. Game Recap The Buffalo Bills defense came up when it mattered most on Thursday night. Backed up at their own 11-yard line with 26 seconds left in the fourth quarter, the Kansas City Chiefs needed one first down to run out the rest of the clock and force overtime. QB Patrick Mahomes fumbled the first-down snap, losing five yards back to the six. A five-yard rush was followed up by an incompletion, forcing a punt on fourth down backed up in their own end zone. ILB Joe Andreeseen got a hand on the punt, giving Chiefs P Matt Araiza 45 yards of distance. WR Greg Dortch picked up 17 yards on the return, leaving just four seconds on the clock. Buffalo trotted out K Tyler Bass for a 57-yard attempt in the wind and the rain, drilling it through the uprights as time expired for a walkoff 13-10 victory on Thanksgiving Night. The first quarter featured zero points, becoming the first Josh Allen and Mahomes matchup to start with four consecutive punts.

items.body: NEWS ANNOUNCEMENTS 'We've got to be at our best' | Buffalo's offense gears up to take on the Kansas City Chiefs' stifling defense Nov 26, 2026 at 08:45 AM Mike Maynard Seasonal Writing Associate Copied! Caean Couto/Buffalo Bills Buffalo Bills vs Kansas City Chiefs, Regular Season, November 02, 2025 at Highmark Stadium. Riding a six-game winning streak, the Buffalo Bills enter arguably their most highly anticipated matchups of the season. The rival Kansas City Chiefs are coming into town for a Thanksgiving Night clash, boasting an 8-2 record and one of the NFL's best defenses. Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has led a consistently dominant defense ever since taking over in 2019, second in points allowed per game (19.8) since then. 2026 has been another great year for Spagnuolo's unit, allowing the second-fewest points per game (16.3) through the first 10 games of the season. "He's done it at the highest level and in the biggest moments," Brady said of Spagnuolo. "You watch in Super Bowl performances how he dials it up. He does an incredible job of understanding his tendencies, and he keeps you on your toes of it all. What he puts on tape, he always has changeups with it. "He's lived in moments of dialing it up in critical situations and also lived in moments where you're thinking he's going to dial it up, and he flips it on you. It's always a chess match going against him, and that's what makes him so great." Deception has been at the forefront of what's given Kansas City's defenses so much success in recent memory, making it a difficult team to game plan for. The Bills have seen Spagnuolo defenses 10 times since he landed with the Chiefs, understanding the headaches that he can create for opponents.

items.body: The Panthers' linebacker depth and experience is proving crucial during important stretch Devin Lloyd, Bobby Okereke, and Tyrel Dodson were added with intent this offseason. And now, it's paying off, as the group deals with injuries but hasn't missed a beat during an important stretch of games. Nov 27, 2026 at 05:42 PM Kassidy Hill Copied! Sarah Boeke/Carolina Panthers Linebacker Tyrel Dodson (33) and linebacker Devin Lloyd are seen during Carolina Panthers practice Thursday, Nov 5, 2026 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, NC. CHARLOTTE â Dan Morgan planned for this. Going back to March, when he began building a new linebacker corps for the Carolina Panthers, he was accumulating talent and personnel for a situation like this: a starter injured for multiple weeks and the defense moving forward without a blip. Devin Lloyd â added in March as the star of the free agency class â was, is, and will continue to be the center of this defense and, therefore, the linebacker unit as well. "I think Devin and Jaelan Phillips are two guys that we obviously held in high regard during free agency," Morgan said at the time. "When you look at both those guys physically, how big they are, how long they are, the effort that they play with, the way they prepare, they were definitely guys that we had our eyes on during free agency. "Me being a former player and watching them on tape, they have everything that you want in terms of the motor, the effort, the instincts, the range that they play with.

The team opened the practice window for outside linebacker Thomas Incoom on Wednesday, as they prepared for this week's game against the Buccaneers. Incoom, 27, led the Panthers with 16 special teams tackles in 2025, and he had three special teams tackles and a fumble recovery in five games this season. He was placed on IR heading into Week 7 with a calf injury. That gives him three weeks to practice, and he'd still need to be added back to the active roster to appear in a game.â Teams have eight spots a year to activate players from injured reserve, and Incoom is the seventh. That leaves one, ostensibly for cornerback Jaycee Horn . Teams can only get more spots if they make the playoffs, when they'd have the ability to bring two more back.

Plus Jalen Coker cleared, and other updates from Monday. Nov 23, 2026 at 02:41 PM by Darin Gantt & Kassidy Hill Copied! CHARLOTTE â The key to Tell the Truth Monday is to do it after big wins the same way you do it after tough losses. It's easy to point out mistakes after a loss, because there are generally more of them. But when they looked back on the win against the Ravens, Panthers head coach Dave Canales said they saw between 15 and 18 missed tackles, depending on who was counting. The Panthers allowed 421 yards of total offense, which made it hard to fully appreciate the three turnovers they created on defense. "Defensively speaking, while it was physical, we had a bunch of missed tackles," Canales said. "We had, debatable whether it was between 15 and 18 missed tackles early on. We settled down in the second half. That really changed the course of it." Canales said they emphasize tackling technique in practice anyway, and the Ravens have something to do with this (Derrick Henry is harder to bring down than most). "That all has to be factored into the fact that we know who they are, we know what they're going to try to do," he said. "We need to get there with urgency." The good news is they have guys out there creating turnovers, like cornerback Will Lee III , and guys on the other end, like Tyrel Dodson , ready to collect. "T-Dot has been amazing for us, and he brings a lot of experience," Canales said. "He studies film. He seems to know what's happening. He's got great instincts, and the fact that he flies to the ball is what creates those opportunities.

Loveland sustained the injury in the first quarter while blocking on a running play. The No. 10 pick in the first round of the 2025 draft is third on the Bears in receiving with 41 receptions for 397 yards and is tied for second with three touchdown catches â all in the last six games. Loveland has started all 11 contests this season and appeared in 16 of 17 games last year, missing a Week 3 win over the Cowboys with a hip issue. In 2025, he became the first rookie to lead the Bears in receiving yards (713) since Willie Gault in 1983 and the first rookie tight end to do so since Hall of Famer Mike Ditka in 1961. In a wild card win over the Packers, Loveland caught eight passes for 137 yards to become the first rookie tight end in NFL history with at least eight receptions and 100 yards in a postseason game.

items.body: Bears mourn loss of Martha Firestone Ford Nov 26, 2026 at 08:33 AM Larry Mayer Senior Writer Copied! Martha Firestone Ford and Virginia Halas McCaskey Detroit Lions owner/chair emeritus Martha Firestone Ford passed away at her home surrounded by her family Tuesday at the age of 101. "Mrs. Ford was a stalwart of our League," Bears chairman George H. McCaskey said in a statement. "She guided the Lions quietly and steadily. Her philanthropic and community support of the greater Detroit area had no bounds. "Mrs. Ford was a fierce competitor and dear friend. She and Virginia McCaskey spoke often and fondly of sitting together in the stands for Lions-Bears games at Tiger Stadium and at Wrigley Field â something unheard of in today's NFL. "Tomorrow, when we play the Lions on Thanksgiving at Ford Field, Mrs. Ford will be on our minds and in our hearts. We extend our condolences to Sheila, the Ford and Firestone families, and to the Pride." Mrs. Ford was a longtime friend of Bears owner Virginia Halas McCaskey, who passed away Feb. 6, 2025, at the age of 102. The two were among four female NFL owners featured in the 2019 documentary "A Lifetime of Sundays," which offered an in-depth look at NFL history from their unique perspective as the league prepared to celebrate its 100th season. The other two female owners were the Chiefs' Norma Hunt and the Steelers' Patricia Rooney. One scene in "A Lifetime of Sundays" shows Mrs. McCaskey and Mrs. Ford catching up inÂ a suite at Ford Field beforeÂ a Bears-Lions Thanksgiving game.Â Coincidentally, the two teams will meet again on Thanksgiving this week in Detroit. "They come by every time we play them, and Mrs. McCaskey always brings us a box of chocolates," Mrs. Ford says in the documentary. "We've been pals for so many years.

items.body: Thanksgiving showdown will be a full-circle moment for Caleb Williams Nov 26, 2026 at 08:31 AM Larry Mayer Senior Writer Copied! Madelaina Polk/Chicago Bears The winner of the nationally televised Bears-Lions showdown Thanksgiving Day in Detroit will move into sole possession of first place in the NFC North. It's exactly the type of game that quarterback Caleb Williams would dream of playing while growing up in and around Washington, D.C. "It's awesome," Williams said. "It's always easier to get up for these games. As a kid, you were sitting at home watching this with your parents, your pops. Me at least, I was sitting home watching these games with my pops, eating some food that my mom made. And so, to be able to be in this position, it's awesome, it's fun. "As a competitor, as a team that wants to go and strive for greatness, you've got to go on the road, and you've got to be able to go out and win these battles. So, it's going to be a great challenge for us as a team; execution on a super short week and then being able to go in somebody else's home and find a way to come out with the win." Speaking to reporters Tuesday, Williams reminisced about watching Thanksgiving games with his dad, munching on chips dipped in creamed spinach. "It's great memories," said the Bears quarterback. "Now I get to be a part of making memories for somebody else.

Monday evening at Soldier Field was all about honoring the top 1% of Illinois high school girls flag football players. Just a day after the legendary stadium was packed with fans for the Bears' 21-13 win over the Saints, 56 student-athletes and their families gathered in the United Club to celebrate a victory of their own â being named to the 2026 All-State girls flag football team.â View this post on Instagram The All-State dinner, supported by Gatorade and Visa, is an annual tradition the Bears started after the 2023 flag football season to recognize athletes' outstanding achievements and the sport's impact. This year, the All-State selection committee faced its biggest challenge yet, needing to select just 56 out of nearly 10,000 student-athletes across 240 teams that played flag football in Illinois this season. "It's an honor and a pleasure to recognize the Chicago Bears Girls Flag Football All-State team," director of youth football development Gustavo Silva said. "This is the fourth All-State team, and as the sport continues to grow, it gets more difficult to select the team and more difficult for the girls to make the team. The level of play, the competition, the skill sets of the players and the coaching continue to elevate, and it's amazing to watch." "This has grown every single year, and it is really exciting. items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: After Further Review Bears rookie Zavion Thomas displays triple-threat ability Nov 23, 2026 at 04:05 PM Larry Mayer Senior Writer Copied! Jacob Funk/Chicago Bears Bears receiver Zavion Thomas delivered the most impactful game of his rookie season in Sunday's 21-13 victory over the Saints. The third-round pick displayed his triple-threat ability with a 30-yard run, 40-yard catch and 29-yard kickoff return. In the process, Thomas became the first Bears player with a 30-plus-yard run and 40-plus-yard reception in the same game since running back Matt Forte Nov. 4, 2012, in a win over the Titans. "He's a player that continues to learn and we get more trust in every week," said coach Ben Johnson, who revealed that Thomas has been "working behind the scenes" with receivers coach/assistant head coach Antwaan Randle El and offensive quality control coach Isaiah Ford. "They're spending a lot of extra time with him. So, you see over the course of a week of practice that he's more on it. As a result, the coaches and his teammates have more trust in him. His package of plays that he goes into a game with, it's going to continue to grow. "We know how much of a playmaker he can be when the ball gets in his hands. [He has] elite speed. I think for a guy that fast, it's really impressive how well he can track the ball and has natural hands when it comes to that. I think we'll continue to see where it goes. He's got a really bright future." items.headline: Celebrating Women and Girls in Sports: How Phoebe Schecter is helping the Bears grow flag football internationally
items.summary: In honor of the Bears' Celebrating Women and Girls in Sports game Sunday at Soldier Field, ChicagoBears.com profiles Phoebe Schecter, an international flag football player, former captain of the Great Britain women's national American football team, former NFL assistant coach and contributor to Sky Sports' NFL coverage, who has been an ardent supporter of the Bears’ efforts to expand flag football
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: Celebrating Women and Girls in Sports: How Phoebe Schecter is helping the Bears grow flag football internationally Nov 21, 2026 at 08:28 PM Gabby Hajduk Writer Copied! Team Great Britain flag football player. NFL global flag football ambassador. Sky Sports NFL analyst. Flag football coach. Mentor. Role model. Chicago Bears partner. If someone had told Phoebe Schecter â now a celebrity in the United Kingdom â 14 years ago that all of those roles now describe her, she would have simply laughed and moved on with her day. After uprooting her life at 22 and moving from her home in Connecticut to the United Kingdom to pursue an equestrian career â something she had worked her entire life for â the idea that her world would soon center on football would have seemed preposterous. Sports were never a big part of Schecter's life growing up, let alone a physical, demanding game like football. Her passion was always horses. Not to mention, women or girls playing or coaching football wasn't a widespread opportunity yet â either back home in the States or in England. Schecter grew up with dual citizenship, her father American and her mother English, giving her familiarity with the UK, yet a year into living there by herself, she craved community and a taste of home. Something about American football spoke to her in that moment. It was an activity that would check both of those boxes. A big believer in taking risks and stepping outside one's comfort zone to find answers, Schecter tried out for an American football team in Manchester. From that day on, she was hooked. "I honestly don't think my 10- or 12-year-old self ever would think this would be me," Schecter said.

items.headline: Game Within The Game | Joe Burrow Feels A Brees As He Challenges NFL Record
items.summary: Joe Burrow doesn’t have to check his phone. Ask him if he knows the NFL record for completion percentage in a season, and he spits it out like the coverages he expects to see Sunday from the Saints (1 p.m.-Cincinnati’s Local 12) at Paycor Stadium.
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: Game Within The Game | Joe Burrow Feels A Brees As He Challenges NFL Record Nov 27, 2026 at 06:22 PM Geoff Hobson Bengals.com Senior Writer Copied! No. 9 has a number indivisible by immortality. Joe Burrow doesn't have to check his phone. Ask him if he knows the NFL record for completion percentage in a season, and he spits it out like the coverages he expects to see Sunday from the Saints (1 p.m.-Cincinnati's Local 12) at Paycor Stadium. "Seventy-four point four," Burrow will tell you. He knows it because his idol, his No. 9 Bayou soulmate, set it when Drew Brees broke his own record in 2018. That was the last time the Saints were here, when Brees Rembrandted the Paycor landscape with 25 passes for an 88 completion percentage on the way to 74.4, besting his 72% from the year before. "I heard about that game," says Burrow, who by then was beginning his LSU career that put him in the Louisiana pantheon with Brees. That would have been 22 of 25 for 265 yards and three touchdowns, which sounds an awful lot like Joe Burrow, circa 2026, where Burrow sits atop the NFL with a 74.2 completion percentage. "What's amazing is how many times he's thrown the football," says Ken Anderson, the Bengals Ring of Honor member who is the first word in quarterback accuracy. "For Joe to do it with the amount of attempts he has, it's unbelievable." What we have here are the three best marksmen from their generation. From the end of World War II to the first year of the Obama Administration, Anderson was the only NFL quarterback to hit 70 percent at 70.55. (Anderson set the record in the nine games of the 1982 strike-shortened season. He threw nearly twice as many passes as record-setting Sammy Baugh did in 1945 when he stunned the NFL by hitting 218 of 309 passes.

items.headline: Quick Hits | Joe Burrow Keeps Throwing; D.J. Turner II's Short Memory
items.summary: A vignette: This is why Joe Burrow is Joe Burrow.
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: Quick Hits | Joe Burrow Keeps Throwing; D.J. Turner II's Short Memory Nov 25, 2026 at 09:02 PM Geoff Hobson Bengals.com Senior Writer Copied! A vignette: This is why Joe Burrow is Joe Burrow. It is 5:45 p.m. Wednesday, and his Bengals teammates have been in the locker room for about 15 minutes after their walkthrough. The wind is blowing, and the temperature has to be damn near in the 30s on the night before Thanksgiving, and there is Burrow throwing to quarterbacks coach Brad Kragthorpe and his assistant Jordan Salkin as their lonely figures cut the ghostly glow of a Paycor Stadium dusk. It is less than 48 hours after the loss in Washington, a game in which Burrow couldn't come up with that final third-down conversion to keep the ball away from Jayden Daniels. And he is throwing. He'll go from there right to his weekly news briefing. "Trying to get better," said Burrow, when asked if there was anything specific he was working on. "Just trying to get better." Rookie wide receiver Colbie Young caught the second of Burrow's two touchdown passes Monday night, the first of his career and the NFL-leading 29 th for Burrow. "He takes pride to the next level, and we feed off him," Young said. "It starts with him. When his energy is up and he's flying around, this offense is a freight train moving on him. He's in here early taking care of his body. No complacency. The longer the season goes, the earlier he gets in. We're just following him. He wants it bad. That's why the energy on this team is so high." Offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher knows exactly how his guy is wired. "I think Joe holds himself to as high or higher standard than anybody else holds him to," Pitcher said.

items.headline: Game Within The Game | Zac Taylor's Coaching Collaboration Defines Bengals' Hottest Offense In All The Land
items.summary: The hottest offense in the world, and what appears to be the most collaborative, met for the last time Saturday before their trip to Washington for Monday night’s game against the Commanders, and, as usual, passing game coordinator Justin Rascati had the last word.
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: Game Within The Game | Zac Taylor's Coaching Collaboration Defines Bengals' Hottest Offense In All The Land Nov 21, 2026 at 06:23 PM Geoff Hobson Bengals.com Senior Writer Copied! The hottest offense in the world, and what appears to be the most collaborative, met for the last time Saturday before their trip to Washington for Monday night's game (8:15-ESPN, Cincinnati's Channel 5) against the Commanders, and, as usual, passing game coordinator Justin Rascati had the last word. That's because he's in charge of the red zone offense, where Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow leads the NFL from inside the 20-yard line with 20 touchdown passes, 76.5 completion percentage, and 293 yards, and like most head coaches, Zac Taylor installs red zone in the last practice of the week. Like the pass protection meeting that running back coach Justin Hill always runs the day before, it lasts about 30 minutes. Hill's get-togethers, which are spent primarily on third down and come under the umbrella of third-down chief Brad Kragthorpe, the quarterbacks coach, have also been mega productive. Up until last week, the Bengals had been converting third downs at a rate not seen since Drew Brees and his 2011 Saints. Even after going 2-for-7 against the Steelers, they're still at 51.9%, .1 behind the NFL-leading 49ers. "When you combine great play calls with great quarterback play," says tight end Mike Gesicki, "that's Â what you're going to get." The ego-less Taylor is mirroring what the late Sam Wyche did when he coached the Bengals to the 1990 AFC Central title and within five minutes of the AFC title game without an offensive coordinator. He called it "a melting pot of ideas," with his coaching staff contributing to playcalling.

items.body: Quick Hits | Bengals Hope To Handle Commanders' Blitz; Burrow Loves To Watch T. Dex Nov 20, 2026 at 06:48 PM Geoff Hobson Bengals.com Senior Writer Copied! After Joe Burrow confirmed he felt much better, prefers spicy food when he's ill, and doesn't seem to be as sick as when Athens High School lost to Wellston in a long-ago basketball game, on Friday the NFL's hottest quarterback turned his attention to Monday night's game (8:15-ESPN, Cincinnati's Channel 5) in Washington. Old friend Daronte Jones, the Commanders defensive Â coordinator who worked for both Bengals head coaches Marvin Lewis and Zac Taylor as an assistant secondary coach, likes to bring the heat. Look at his pedigree. Before he worked for Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores, he got a dose of Vikings head coach Mike Zimmer's double-A gap blitz for a season. No surprise the Commanders have the fourth-highest blitz rate (35.7%) in the NFL, via Pro Football Reference. But will Jones blitz that much Monday night? Nobody has been better against the blitz than Burrow. He's coming off a torrid 12-for-12 for 186 yards against Steelers' pressure last week for 186 yards, and, according to Stat Muse, leads the NFL in passer rating against blitzes (114.8) and passing touchdowns (23), and yards (2,386). "There are two linebackers that are big physical guys that can make you pay in pass protection. They have guys that can rush the passer. They have corners that are big and long and like to take chances, and they're good tacklers also," Burrow said after Friday's practice. "We have to be on our P's and Q's in protection and I've got to know where my hot answers are, and I've got to know where I can get the ball out quickly. Pick up the blitzes.

The Nigerian Secondary School Flag Football League (NSSFFL) is set to engage at least 144 schools across 18 states as it begins its fifth season, strengthening efforts to establish flag football as a sustainable school sport and create pathways for young Nigerian athletes. The competition, organized by the Nigerian American Football Association (NAFA), is expected to feature at least 288 teams across the boys' and girls' divisions, with approximately 2,880 student-athletes participating in the state preliminaries. When WR KC Concepcion Jr. Â was a freshman at NC State, he found success early on the football field. With that success brought the spotlight, and through interviews, he showed the world surrounding collegiate football who he was as a person who has a stutter. Concepcion said he pushed through interviews, continuing to work on becoming more comfortable in that space. At the same time, he put a heavy emphasis on interacting and engaging with fans. So, after games, he would stay and sign every item of kids who sought his autograph â sometimes signing up to 200 items each Saturday of football season. In those interactions with kids, he began to realize that they were not focused on his stutter, but instead, relished in the chance to meet a collegiate athlete they admired. Those interactions with kids, and the opportunity to positively impact their day, brought Concepcion a new level of confidence. "It definitely changed it because I was never really the like outgoing, spoken in the like spotlight all the time," Concepcion said. "And then after my freshman season and just going through my freshman season and just seeing like I could like change lives, I would say that's where the confidence came from." Now as a member of the Browns, Concepcion is continuing to impact the lives of kids through his example. By effectively using his legs, taking care of the football and establishing himself as a leader on a young Browns' team, Watson has played a critical role in Cleveland's 6-4 start to the season. "I always knew who I was and I always knew what I was about," Watson said. "That's why I just block out, even the success. I try to stay neutral, just try to stay poised and focus on what really matters and that's just finding ways to get better in my career." items.headline: Brian Schottenheimer, Cowboys 'ready to get back to work' after Thanksgiving loss to Eagles
items.summary: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said he had conversations with Jerry and Stephen Jones following Dallas' 39-38 loss to the Eagles on Thursday that "were shared disappointment," but that he and the team are "ready to get back to work."
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: Featured - PHIvsDAL | 2026 Presented by Brian Schottenheimer, Cowboys 'ready to get back to work' after Thanksgiving loss to Eagles Nov 27, 2026 at 12:58 PM Tommy Yarrish DallasCowboys.com Staff Writer Copied! FRISCO, Texas â Cowboys owner/GM Jerry Jones used the word "numbing" to describe Dallas' 39-38 loss to the Eagles on Thanksgiving. On a conference call Friday, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said he spoke to both Jerry Jones and COO/co-owner Stephen Jones Thursday night following the loss. "They share in our disappointment," Schottenheimer said of his conversations with the Jones family. "Again, we felt like we had an opportunity to win that game. An important game, divisional game against a division rival. Our conversations were shared disappointment, but also, we're ready to get back to work." The Cowboys now have an 11-day break between games ahead of their Week 13 matchup on the road against the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Over the extended week, Schottenheimer said special teams is one area the team will spend time on. "Certainly, we need to find out some of the things on special teams," Schottenheimer said. "Just a couple of the big returns that got away from us. Some of those things. The blocked punt too was a big play in the game, so we'll spend quite a bit of time looking at that. Again, this is a chance for us to really look at all 12 games and kind of see where we are and take a very cumulative approach to this and get ready for these last five." One of the changes the Cowboys have made this season is at defensive play-caller, with senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine taking over play-calling from defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Thursday's game was the second game that Pettine has called this season.

items.headline: Special teams errors loom large in Cowboys' 39-38 loss to Eagles
items.summary: A blocked punt for a touchdown, a missed field goal and a big kickoff return, all in the fourth quarter, played a big role on Thursday in the Cowboys' 39-38 loss to the Eagles.
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: Featured - PHIvsDAL | 2026 Presented by Special teams errors loom large in Cowboys' 39-38 loss to Eagles Nov 26, 2026 at 10:46 PM Tommy Yarrish DallasCowboys.com Staff Writer Copied! ARLINGTON, Texas â After the Cowboys' 39-38 loss to the Eagles on Sunday, coach Brian Schottenheimer said all three phases of the game had a hand in Dallas' Thanksgiving day loss. For the third phase of the game on special teams, a majority of their errors came in the second half. The first was a blocked punt on Bryan Anger by Eagles DT Ty Robinson with 13:53 left in the fourth quarter, which was scooped up by Kenny Moore and returned for a touchdown to cut Dallas' lead to 31-24. "The blocked punt was big, obviously," Schottenheimer said. "But like I said, we had a chance with the ball in our hand offensively to put the game away and we didn't. And all three phases had a hand in this one." Like I said, division games, you should expect this game to go down to the wire like that. "We've got to get more points than we did, and we didn't." The loss is accountable to the offense, true, but also to the defense and special teams â making it a failure on all fronts. items.summary: The Cowboys again have a bad defense, yet people blame Dak Prescott. I was just curious if that drives you guys as crazy as it drives me. Dak has had his bad moments this season, but he's the absolute least of this team's problems.

(Editor's Note: Time to check the mail! The DallasCowboys.com staff writers answer your questions here in 'Mailbag' presented by Miller Lite.) The Cowboys again have a bad defense, yet people blame Dak Prescott. I was just curious if that drives you guys as crazy as it drives me. Dak has had his bad moments this season, but he's the absolute least of this team's problems. â Â Ralph Gruendel / Bloomfield, NJ Nick: Â Well, let's be honest about one part â he's the highest-paid player in the history of the NFL. So that has to be mentioned first because I'm sure he gets judged by that. No other quarterback has topped $60 million per season and so, considering he hasn't won the big game or really gotten his team close to that, Dak is going to be linked to that contract â fair or not. But I've learned to just accept that criticism is always going to follow the quarterback of the Dallas Cowboys. I never could understand why an undrafted QB from Eastern Illinois jumped into the scene and played the way he did â and still got the criticism Tony Romo did. And now, you've got a guy who was a fourth-round pick, thrown into the fire from the start, has played as long as he has and been a really good player with just about every passing record known to man for the Cowboys. And then when you factor in that Dak is one of the most likable players in the NFL, it's always weird if he gets a lot of negative criticism his way. But I like to be fair about everything. I enjoyed watching Romo. I enjoy watching Dak. I think they're both great players. But I don't look at their careers being wasted because they didn't win.

The defensive showing against the Titans wasn't perfect, allowing 30 points, something that drew the ire of All-Pro Quinnen Williams , but the defensive unit did rack up five sacks against Cam Ward, forced two fumbles and recovered to help the high-powered Cowboys get back in the win column. And, equally as important, there were no distractions â something Parker insisted would not be an issue. "Other than pushing a button and calling the play, [Parker] was very involved in talking to Pet," Schottenheimer added.

items.body: Featured - TENvsDAL | 2026 Presented by Brian Schottenheimer 'very proud' of Cowboys defense in Mike Pettine's first game as play-caller Nov 22, 2026 at 06:00 PM Tommy Yarrish DallasCowboys.com Staff Writer Copied! ARLINGTON, Texas â The Cowboys defense was in the headlines all week, as Brian Schottenheimer announced senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine would take over as Dallas' defensive play-caller, while Christian Parker remained the defensive coordinator. In his first game calling plays since being the Packers DC in 2020, the Pettine-called Cowboys defense gave up 30 points and 346 yards to the Titans on Sunday in a 51-30 win for Dallas. It wasn't all pretty, but Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer was happy with the unit's performance. "Very proud," Schottenheimer said. "Very proud of those guys. I think the first half was outstanding, but I thought they did a great job of blocking out the noise and working. I was really excited for how they performed." In the first half, the Cowboys did not allow the Titans into the end zone and held Tennessee's offense to three points. As a whole, the Cowboys defense held Tennessee to 3 of 10 third down conversions, sacked Cam Ward five times and were +1 in the turnover battle of a strip sack from Quinnen Williams that was scooped up by Markquese Bell. One additional adjustment Dallas made defensively this week? Simplifying things on defense. Schottenheimer said the "menu was a little bit tighter" referring to defensive play calls this week, which seemed to lead to better execution at times. "We were moving some pieces around and using guys different ways, but overall we talked all week about trying to do simple better and trying to tackle and communicate and take care of the football," Schottenheimer said.

ENGLEWOOD, Colo. â Â The Broncos are headed to the home of the Terrible Towel. In their upcoming Black Friday matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, the Broncos will travel to Acrisure Stadium âÂ and they know the challenge that awaits against the 6-4 Steelers. "This is one of those spots you want to play a road game at," quarterback Bo Nix said Tuesday. "This is one of the places that's historic, well known for their environment. I'm excited for the atmosphere, excited to experience it and be in the moment and go out here and play a really good competitive football team. We have to play well. We have to show up, and we have to be prepared." The signature yellow towels will swirl Friday afternoon, and Head Coach Sean Payton pointed to the advantage that the crowd noise can provide a dangerous Pittsburgh pass rush that's led by four-time first-team All-Pro and former Defensive Player of the Year T.J. Watt. "They're really good edge players, especially if they can get you behind the chains," Payton said. "It's one of the strengths, and it has been. So, yes, there's the challenge again to the right and those guys to the left the same way. So, we just have to be on the protection plan and especially on the road. [It's] a little bit easier to dial up some of those pressures when that [quarterback's] foot goes up in the air compared to when you're at home with a little bit better way to [snap the ball].

items.body: Notebook Presented by NOTEBOOK: Scruggs anchoring Lions' offensive line Nov 24, 2026 at 05:22 PM Tim Twentyman Senior Writer Copied! Where would the Detroit Lions' offense be without offensive lineman Juice Scruggs ? It's a fair question given the way he's played the center position this season and with the recent news of Cade Mays going on injured reserve with an ankle injury. Mays was signed this offseason to be the team's center. Scruggs came to Detroit as part of the David Montgomery trade this offseason. To start training camp, Mays was the starter and Scruggs rotated between center and guard, competing for a role. When Mays suffered a wrist injury in camp, Scruggs moved into the starting center role. "Yeah, I really can't say enough great things about (Scruggs)," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said Tuesday. "He's just been a great addition for us. He's a pro. He's the same guy every day. He's very consistent. He doesn't ride the wave, the ups and downs. He's positive. He goes to work, makes corrections, plays snap to whistle, hustles, great teammate. He's everything." Scruggs started at center the first five games of the season and played terrific, holding down the fort for Mays' return, which came Week 7 vs. Green Bay. Mays suffered an ankle injury in Week 8 against Minnesota, putting Scruggs back into the center spot. He's been even better in his second stint as the starter the last three games, allowing just three total pressures in wins over Miami, New England and Tampa Bay. "The culture that (Campbell's) built here, I would say it just fits my style of play," Scruggs said Tuesday of why Detroit's been such a good fit for him since coming over from Houston.

items.headline: KEY QUESTIONS: How are Lions approaching quick turnaround to Thanksgiving game?
items.summary: Tim Twentyman covers all the key questions from Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell's Monday press conference.
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: KEY QUESTIONS: How are Lions approaching quick turnaround to Thanksgiving game? Nov 23, 2026 at 06:55 PM Tim Twentyman Senior Writer Copied! Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell spoke to the media on Monday one day after his team's 31-21 victory over Tampa Bay that extended their win streak to six games and improves their record to an NFC-North-leading 8-2. Campbell, his staff and the players were back at the Meijer Performance Center on Monday as they prepare for a quick turnaround against the Chicago Bears (8-2) on Thanksgiving at Ford Field. This matchup will decide first place in the the division following Week 12 as both teams currently hold the same record. Here are all the key questions from Campbell's Monday press conference: What jumps out about the Bears on tape? Like Detroit, the Bears are a hot team. They've won five straight and have not trailed in any of those five games. Campbell has a lot of respect for the job head coach Ben Johnson and his staff have done in Chicago and is expecting a terrific matchup on a national stage on Thursday. Campbell said quarterback Caleb Williams is a 'heck of a player' and dynamic with the ball in his hands. He mentioned wide receiver Luther Burden III, tight end Colston Loveland and running back D'Andre Swift as skill weapons the Lions must look to contain on Thursday. Their offensive line has mostly stayed intact this season and that's been huge for that side of the ball, per Campbell. Chicago ranks eighth in scoring (26.2), eighth in total offense (375.8), third in rushing (142.4) and 14th in passing (233.4). He's seen growth from Chicago's defense in the second season of Dennis Allen's system. Campbell thinks Jeffrey Simmons has been a terrific addition to the defensive line and makes everyone around him better.

items.summary: Packers struggle to stop Blake Corum, lose WR Christian Watson to concussion

items.body: Game notes: Grateful to be back, Micah Parsons addresses disappointing defeat in L.A. Packers struggle to stop Blake Corum, lose WR Christian Watson to concussion Nov 26, 2026 at 12:30 AM Wes Hodkiewicz packers.com senior writer Copied! Keller Nienau, packers.com EDGE Micah Parsons INGLEWOOD, Calif. â Micah Parsons was filled with mixed feelings in the aftermath of his highly anticipated return Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Rams. On one hand, Parsons felt healthy and strong while recording two quarterback hits and a sack in his first NFL game since tearing the anterior cruciate ligament and meniscus in his right knee 346 days ago in Denver. While grateful to get through the game unscathed, Parsons also felt disappointment after coming up short during a 26-13 road loss to the Rams in Week 12 tilt at SoFi Stadium. Knowing full well Los Angeles wanted to establish the run without star receivers Davante Adams and Puka Nacua, Green Bay still struggled to contain the Rams' one-two punch of Blake Corum (32 carries for 184 yards and a touchdown) and Kyren Williams (12-46-1 TD) over four quarters. The Rams controlled the ball for more than 40 minutes and nearly rushed for as many yards (241) on the ground as the Packers had in total (244). "We all saw that game, and we saw where we got exploited at," Parsons said. "It starts with us. It starts with up front. It's not pointing fingers at things but when runs open up like the Red Sea, we gotta look at ourselves in the mirror regardless of how that is. We have to do a better job collectively up front." Green Bay kept a lid on the Rams' offense early, limiting it to two Brandon McManus field goals in the first quarter despite a sudden-change situation in Packers' territory.

items.body: Justin Friske of Pewaukee High School named WFCA/Packers High School Coach of the Year Friske led his Pirates to a perfect 14-0 record, culminating in a 24-7 victory over Port Washington in the WIAA Division 3 state championship game Nov 25, 2026 at 03:54 PM Copied! Back row (left to right): Jeff Grabo, Eric Austin, Justin Friske (Head Coach) Casey Vullings; Middle row (left to right): Nic Hall, Sean Hegarty, Kyle Haug, Kellen Figueroa, Matt Farra; Front row (left to right): Mike Lecher Sr., Joe Grabo, Mike Lecher Jr., Sam Anderson Justin Friske of Pewaukee High School in Pewaukee, Wis., has been named the Wisconsin Football Coaches Association (WFCA)/Green Bay Packers High School Coach of the Year. In his 15th season as head coach at Pewaukee, Friske led his Pirates to a perfect 14-0 record, culminating in a 24-7 victory over Port Washington in the WIAA Division 3 state championship game at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison. This championship is the team's second state title under Friske, who previously led his Pirates to a state championship in 2021. This year's title means a great deal to Friske, his players and the Pewaukee community, and he is proud of how they delivered on their commitment to excellence. "We have a lot of people who invest a ton of their time and energy into making sure our kids can have the very best experiences possible, and we have a very talented group of young men who have bought into our mission, goals and aspirations of our athletic department and football program," said Friske. "To be honored this way, being able to celebrate a state championship, is validation for all the hard work and effort everyone has put in, as well as fulfillment of the commitment we've all made to each other.

items.body: Packers list eight questionable vs. Rams | Week 12 Injury Report EDGE Micah Parsons, RB Josh Jacobs among those questionable for Thanksgiving Eve Nov 24, 2026 at 12:00 PM Wes Hodkiewicz packers.com senior writer Copied! Emma Pravecek, packers.com EDGE Micah Parsons GREEN BAY â The Packers have listed edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee) among eight players who are questionable for Wednesday night's game against the Los Angeles Rams. The other seven questionable are running back Josh Jacobs (finger), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps), guard/tackle Travis Glover (shoulder) and receivers Bo Melton (thigh) and Skyy Moore (ankle). Parsons is currently on the physically unable to perform list and will need to be activated to the 53-man roster by Wednesday when his 21-day practice window closes. Parsons returned to practice on Nov. 4, his first on-field action since tearing his anterior cruciate ligament and meniscus last December against Denver. He's been a limited participant in practice since then. "It wasn't as bad as I thought," said Parsons on Monday about his ramp-up period. "Obviously you're limited in the plays consecutively, but I think when you approach your rehab the right way, you kind of really feel really strong about how â when I came out there, I didn't really feel out of breath or feel like I couldn't breathe. I actually felt really solid." Jacobs missed last week's game against Minnesota but returned to practice in a limited capacity Saturday after recently undergoing surgery on the broken ring finger he suffered against New England in Week 9. Head Coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Sunday he didn't expect Jacobs to play in L.A.

items.headline: 'Be Kaleb' mindset has Kaleb Johnson finding his stride
items.summary: Second-year running back gaining comfort, yards for Packers’ offense
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: 'Be Kaleb' mindset has Kaleb Johnson finding his stride Second-year running back gaining comfort, yards for Packers’ offense Nov 23, 2026 at 09:00 AM Wes Hodkiewicz packers.com senior writer Copied! Evan Siegle, packers.com RB Kaleb Johnson GREEN BAY â Kaleb Johnson hasn't exactly had much downtime since being traded to the Packers a week before the start of the regular season. The second-year running back really wouldn't have it any other way. Despite Green Bay having shorter bye week than usual due to its Thanksgiving eve matchup with the Los Angeles Rams this upcoming Wednesday, Johnson was counting down the days until the team reported back to work last Friday. The brief amount of time that Johnson had off consisted of just three things: Family, football and Grand Theft Auto VI. "Staying home, over-studying â slash playing GTA 6," said Johnson, who's already through the third chapter of the recently released video game. "Just allowing your mind to relax, but at the same time stay on top of the game." The 23-year-old running back rode a wave of momentum into the Week 11 bye after providing a needed spark for a Packers run game that struggled to get going during the first half of the season. Acquired in a late August trade with Pittsburgh, the 6-foot-1, 224-pound running back was mainly off the radar before rushing for 110 yards and a touchdown on 24 carries in Green Bay's last two games before the bye. That production has propelled Johnson into becoming the Packers' leading rusher with 214 yards on the season. Yet, NFL Next Gen Stats has credited him for even more yards after contact (216), the fifth-most among running backs with at least 50 rushing attempts this season.

items.body: Packers getting healthier on both sides of the ball Several injured players trending toward returning to action on Thanksgiving eve Nov 21, 2026 at 04:26 PM Mike Spofford packers.com editor Copied! Evan Siegle, packers.com LB Zaire Franklin GREEN BAY â By the time this Thanksgiving eve game rolls around, the Packers just might be the healthiest they've been in a while. Every player on the 53-man roster practiced to some extent Saturday as the team resumed on-field work in preparation for the trip to play the L.A. Rams. Those on the practice field included linebacker Zaire Franklin , offensive linemen Sean Rhyan and Kevin Zeitler , running back Josh Jacobs , and edge rusher Micah Parsons , all of whom have missed significant chunks of the season. Head Coach Matt LaFleur indicated Jacobs, who is dealing with a surgically repaired broken finger, is the least likely to be ready come Wednesday night. But he's not yet being ruled out while the others are trending toward playing provided the next few days go well. "We've got a lot of guys in that boat where they've got to prove it, prove function throughout the course of the week, and they've got to feel confident that they can go out there and get the job done," LaFleur said. For Franklin, his four-game absence due to a "freak accident" that cracked his shin in practice (prior to the Detroit trip late last month) has been difficult personally, as the ninth-year veteran had missed only one game in his entire career previously. The defensive leader and signal caller referred to it as "humbling" to miss so much time because he's accustomed to pushing through whatever might ail him.

Madison Morris, packers.com The Green Bay Packers have signed RB Pierre Strong Jr. to the practice squad and released EDGE D.J. Johnson from the practice squad. General Manager Brian Gutekunst announced the transactions Saturday. Strong (5-11, 207), a fourth-year player out of South Dakota State, has been on the Packers' practice squad and active roster since signing with Green Bay on Sept. 8, 2025, and has played in five games this season, recording 59 yards on 25 carries (2.4 avg.) and 61 yards on 10 receptions (6.1 avg.). He was originally selected in the fourth round (No. 127 overall) of the 2022 NFL Draft by the New England Patriots. Strong played in 46 games with one start for the Patriots (2022) and Cleveland Browns (2023-24), recording 99 carries for 499 yards (5.0 avg.) and two touchdowns. Strong also caught 26 passes for 193 yards (7.4 avg.) and returned 24 kickoffs for 570 yards (23.8 avg.).

items.headline: Why Woody Marks Is the Texans' Pick for Salute to Service Award
items.summary: Woody's family ties to the military led him to host a free football camp for military kids at Fort Hood. Now fans can help vote him into the finalists through Nov. 30.
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: Why Woody Marks Is the Texans' Pick for Salute to Service Award Nov 25, 2026 at 04:09 PM Copied! CRIS ZELAYA/Cristobal Zelaya An image from the November 3rd 2026 Texans Salute to Service Showdown event at Houston Methodist Training Center in Houston, TX. Stay on top of the latest Houston Texans news by adding https://www.houstontexans.com to your Google Source Preferences . The Texans named RB Woody Marks as our nominee for the 2026 Salute to Service Award, and it's well earned. The award honors NFL players, coaches, staff and alumni who show an exceptional commitment to supporting U.S. service members, veterans and their families. For Woody, that commitment shows up in what he does. Woody Marks' military family connection This one is personal for Woody. He grew up with an uncle in the military, and that connection is why he gives back to service members and their families. Now in his second season with the Texans, he's made it a real part of who he is in Houston. A free football camp for military kids at Fort Hood In July, Woody hosted a free, two-day football camp for military children at Fort Hood in Central Texas. The camp wasn't only about football. It gave those kids a chance to come together, make friends, build memories and have fun with other kids who understand what their lives are like. In 2025, Woody was a guest coach in the Texans' Salute to Service Showdown. That's a competitive flag football game between teams representing different branches of the military and first responders. How to vote for Woody Marks for Salute to Service This is where you come in. Voting is open now at NFL.com/SaluteFanVote . You can vote once a day from now through Monday, Nov. 30 to help make Woody one of this year's three finalists. The finalists will be announced in January.
