items.headline: 'Will Is a Dog': Why Will Anderson Jr. Sets the Tone for the Texans Defense
items.summary: DeMeco Ryans called Will Anderson Jr. one of the best players he has been around. C.J. Stroud called him a dog. Even the Colts' head coach called him a problem after the Texans defense kept Indianapolis out of the end zone.
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: 'Will Is a Dog': Why Will Anderson Jr. Sets the Tone for the Texans Defense Nov 20, 2026 at 12:29 PM Copied! JORDAN MCKENDRICK/HOUSTON TEXANS Stay on top of the latest Houston Texans news by adding https://www.houstontexans.com to your Google Source Preferences . DeMeco Ryans on Will Anderson Jr.'s Leadership The Houston Texans defense kept the Indianapolis Colts out of the end zone all night Thursday, and Head Coach DeMeco Ryans pointed straight to DE Will Anderson Jr. "Will has a significant impact on our team not only by the way he plays but just the way he leads," Ryans said. "That's every day. What you see out there on game day is what you see every day, the intensity that he represents, he shows it in practice, he shows it in the meeting room. That's one of the best players I've been around." "From the player and the man, couldn't find a better guy than him and happy for the season he's having, proud of the way he continues to work, remain relentless, represent the way we need to represent. He's having an outstanding year and good things are coming his way." C.J. Stroud: 'The Definition of What You Want for a Texan' QB C.J. Stroud didn't hold back about his teammate. "Will is a dog," Stroud said. "He's the definition of what you want for a Texan. I know DeMeco loves him. I know up top, the ownership loves him. He just works super hard. He doesn't complain and he gets put in tough spots. A lot of times he's getting chipped, getting double-teamed and he's still fighting his tail off, crawling, scratching, doing whatever he can to get to the ball." "Just his tenacity and I think he just brings a swag to this team that I'm just proud to call him my brother.

items.headline: Where Did That Throw Come From? C.J. Stroud Credits Offseason Work for His Strike to Nico Collins
items.summary: DeMeco Ryans said "wow" about C.J. Stroud's touchdown pass to Nico Collins against the Colts, and Stroud gave the credit to the weight room, his teammates and his faith.

items.body: Where Did That Throw Come From? C.J. Stroud Credits Offseason Work for His Strike to Nico Collins Nov 20, 2026 at 10:29 AM Copied! JORDAN MCKENDRICK/HOUSTON TEXANS Stay on top of the latest Houston Texans news by adding https://www.houstontexans.com to your Google Source Preferences . DeMeco Ryans on C.J. Stroud's Touchdown Pass to Nico Collins QB C.J. Stroud's touchdown pass to WR Nico Collins against the Indianapolis Colts left his head coach searching for words. "Yeah, that play to Nico was, I mean, wow. He ripped that one," Head Coach DeMeco Ryans said. "Just watching him and seeing the guys draped on him in the pocket. He really let that one go trusting that Nico. As we always joke about, 'Nico's down there somewhere.' You throw it up, good things will happen. He let that one rip and Nico definitely showed up big time for him making a huge catch." Ryans said Stroud's strength shows up in more than just his arm. "C.J.'s done a great job in the pocket. You see the strength that he has in the pocket, not only throwing, keeping two hands on the ball, being able to escape the rushers, being able to get positive yards rushing the football as well so the strength is definitely showing up." Colts Head Coach Shane Steichen gave Stroud credit too. "Obviously, he made a great play on those throws, stepping up in the pocket," Steichen said. "Hats off to those guys for making those plays." C.J. Stroud Credits the Weight Room and the Strength Staff Stroud pointed to his offseason training and credited Assistant Strength and Conditioning Coach Clint Martin. "I don't know, I've been in the weight room a little bit so maybe credit to that," Stroud said. "Credit to Clint, strength staff and everybody that works with me in that.

items.summary: It's the fifth Thursday night meeting between the Texans and Colts. Here are the numbers that frame Week 11 at Reliant Stadium.

items.body: Texans vs. Colts By the Numbers: Can C.J. Stroud Stay Hot on Thursday Night? Nov 19, 2026 at 03:14 PM John Harris Texans Analyst Copied! JORDAN MCKENDRICK/HOUSTON TEXANS An image from the November 17th, 2026 regular season practice at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. Stay on top of the latest Houston Texans news by adding https://www.houstontexans.com to your Google Source Preferences . Listen to the full episode of Texans All-Access on Spotify or Apple Podcasts . It's Colts week!! Well, kind of. It's a short Colts week as the Texans prepare for the Colts on Thursday night. Since I've been on the sidelines, the Texans have played the Colts on a Thursday night in 2014, 2015, 2019 and now 2026. Add one more in 2011 and it's the fifth Thursday night contest between the two organizations. As such, let's dive into the numbers for this matchup. How the Texans-Colts Rivalry Began 1 â The Texans did not get off to the best start in this rivalry, dating back to 2002. Through the first 16 matchups, the Texans won just once: a Christmas Eve special in 2006 at Reliant Stadium. 19-14-1 â Since that point, the rivalry has been much closer. The Colts still lead over the past 34 games, but the Texans have closed the gap significantly. As a side note, the Colts are the only AFC South team the Texans don't have a series lead againstâ¦but there's still time! A Revolving Door at Colts QB 9 â I've been on the sidelines since 2014, and my first Colts-Texans game was a Thursday nighter when the great Andrew Luck started at QB for Indianapolis.

items.headline: Colts-Giants preview: What to watch for in Anthony Richardson Sr.'s return as starting quarterback
items.summary: Richardson will make his first start since Week 16 of the 2024 season on Sunday against the New York Giants at Lucas Oil Stadium.
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: Game Preview Presented by Colts-Giants preview: What to watch for in Anthony Richardson Sr.'s return as starting quarterback Richardson will make his first start since Week 16 of the 2024 season on Sunday against the New York Giants at Lucas Oil Stadium. Nov 27, 2026 at 09:00 AM JJ Stankevitz Colts.com Writer Copied! If Anthony Richardson Sr. is looking for an example of a quarterback taking advantage of a second chance, all he'll have to do is look across the field at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Since being jettisoned by the Minnesota Vikings for a fourth-round pick in September, JJ McCarthy â a 2024 first-round pick â has quarterbacked the New York Giants to the top of the NFC East with a 6-3-1 record. McCarthy, in his lone year as a starter in Minnesota, completed 57.6 percent of his passes and had a 72.6 passer rating. It's not like McCarthy has blown away opposing defenses in New York â he's completed 59.2 percent of his passes with an 84.5 passer rating â but he's played winning football. The Giants haven't needed McCarthy to be a superstar, but he's stabilized an offense that lost starter Jaxson Dart in Week 2. So can Richardson step in for the Colts, who waived starter Daniel Jones last week, and stabilize an offense that's 26th in points per game (19.2) entering Week 12? "(The) last few days definitely been kind of crazy, especially with everything that's happened to the roster, especially me getting bumped up to QB1," Richardson said. "But I'm blessed. I'm grateful for the opportunity. I'm ready to showcase what I can do and go out there and have fun." Richardson hasn't started a game since Week 16 of the 2024 season.

items.body: Alec Pierce addresses injury recovery, feelings on missing most of Colts' 2026 season: 'It's been really difficult' Pierce, who led the NFL in yards per catch in 2024 and 2025, was placed on injured reserve September. Nov 25, 2026 at 04:39 PM JJ Stankevitz Colts.com Writer Copied! Alec Pierce on Wednesday said he's made good progress over the last few weeks and still hopes to play again in 2026. Whether the 26-year-old wide receiver, who's been on injured reserve since late September, gets back on the field this year remains to be seen. "If I progress well enough, that's kind of my goal, is to get back at some point," Pierce said. "I miss being out there with the guys, I miss being able to help the guys out and add to this offense." Whenever Pierce does return to the Colts â be it during the 2026 or 2027 season â the team surrounding him will look and feel awfully different from the last snap he took against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 2. items.body: Colts DE Caden Curry to miss remainder of 2026 season The Colts placed Curry on injured reserve Tuesday. Nov 25, 2026 at 11:53 AM JJ Stankevitz Colts.com Writer Copied! Colts defensive end Caden Curry will miss the remainder of his rookie season due to a wrist injury, head coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday. Curry sustained a ligament tear in his wrist in the Colts' Week 11 loss to the Houston Texans that required surgery. He was placed on injured reserve Tuesday. The Colts selected Curry in the sixth round (No. 214 overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft, and the Center Grove High School alum roundly impressed coaches and teammates this season. Curry appeared in 11 games and totaled 26 tackles, on sack, one tackle for a loss, two quarterback hits and two fumble recoveries; he also made a significant impact on special teams. Entering Week 12, Curry's 90.7 Pro Football Focus special teams grade ranked fourth among players with at least 100 special teams snaps. "Really unfortunate situation for him," Steichen said. "He was playing at a really high level defensively (and on) special teams. The relentless motor that he played with, the passion that he played with was phenomenal. I know he's going to attack his rehab the right way and be ready to go this offseason."

items.body: Shane Steichen explains Colts' decision to start Anthony Richardson Sr., waive Daniel Jones Colts head coach Shane Steichen answered questions on Friday about the move from Daniel Jones to Anthony Richardson Sr. Nov 20, 2026 at 02:14 PM JJ Stankevitz Colts.com Writer Copied! Head coach Shane Steichen said Friday the Colts' decision to not just remove Daniel Jones as starting quarterback, but also to waive him, was "made for the best interests of both parties." Jones did not request to be released, Steichen said. And moving from Jones to Anthony Richardson Sr. behind center for the Colts' Week 12 game against the New York Giants next weekend was made, Steichen said, because of "where we're at right now in the season." The Colts are 3-8 and have lost six of their last seven games, including three to AFC South opponents. After losing to the previously-winless Tennessee Titans in Week 6, general manager Chris Ballard was dismissed; the Colts lost by a combined 58 points to the Jacksonville Jaguars and Houston Texans in Weeks 8 and 11, respectively. And after losing, 26-3, to the Texans on Thursday, the Colts made a change at quarterback. "I don't think it was just on one person," Steichen said. "I think there's a lot of factors that played into it. Obviously, the quarterback takes a lot of the blame. That's the business that we're in. But things just didn't work out. It didn't work out, and there's a lot of factors for that. And like I said, I got so much respect for him and everything that he meant to this organization and the way he worked." Jones played several games with a broken leg after the Colts' bye week in 2025 before sustaining a season-ending torn Achilles' in Week 14.

items.body: Colts head coach Shane Steichen says he'll 'evaluate everything' after Thursday night trouncing by Texans The Colts lost, 26-3, to the Houston Texans on Thursday night at Reliant Stadium. Nov 20, 2026 at 12:25 AM JJ Stankevitz Colts.com Writer Copied! HOUSTON â Daniel Jones completed four passes that gained at least 20 yards in the first half of the Colts' first appearance on Thursday Night Football since 2022, but that's where the positives ended for the Colts' offense against the Houston Texans. Jones completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards with an interception and a passer rating of 45.9 in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday at Reliant Stadium. He was replaced by backup Anthony Richardson Sr. halfway through the fourth quarter with the Colts down by 23 points. And when asked if Jones would still be his starting quarterback moving forward, Colts head coach Shane Steichen said he'd "evaluate everything." "I thought he could do some things better," Steichen said. "But obviously, there's a good pass rush coming at him. We'll go back and evaluate the tape." Steichen, after the Colts' 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, said the same thing â he'd "evaluate everything" regarding his team, including his starting quarterback. A day after that loss, Steichen announced he'd stick with Jones behind center. Since that loss to the Jaguars, the Colts traded their top two wide receivers (Keenan Allen and Josh Downs) and, on Thursday, played without their starting left tackle (Bernhard Raimann) and their starting right tackle (Jalen Travis).

items.body: Jaguars Wednesday: "So Much Football Left …" Nov 25, 2026 at 05:09 PM John Shipley Jaguars Media Correspondent Copied! JACKSONVILLE â Liam Coen knows what's needed. The AFC South-leading Jaguars will play host to the Tennessee Titans a week after a difficult road loss, with the Jaguars' second-year head coach on Wednesday morning making clear the ideal approach against their division rivals. "A lot about this week for us is so much more about getting back to fundamentally sharp, details and play style," Coen said as the Jaguars (7-3) prepared to play Tennessee Titans (1-9) at EverBank Stadium Sunday. The Jaguars, after three consecutive victories by 17 or more points, lost to the New York Giants 23-18 on the road this past Sunday. They are 5-1 following losses in two seasons under Coen, including 2-0 this season. "We have some good veteran leadership that has played a lot of football and that understands one week doesn't define you," Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence said. "That's true in both cases, whether you're playing really well or whether you're coming off a game where you didn't play your best. It's the same mindset." "We know what we have do to. There's another opportunity this week and we take it personal when we don't play to our standard. That's something that means something to us. When it's not there â like it wasn't Sunday â we're itching to get back out there and prove we can play to our standard." The loss to the Giants snapped a three-game winning streak for a Jaguars team that ranks sixth in the NFL in scoring and ninth in total yards this season. They entered Sunday scoring 30 or more points in four consecutive games, including a 40-23 victory over the Titans on November 15. Their 18 points Sunday were their second lowest of the season.

items.body: Day After Week 11 Loss to Giants: "Settling Back Down…" Nov 23, 2026 at 07:42 PM John Shipley Jaguars Media Correspondent Copied! JACKSONVILLE â The Jaguars must respond. And quickly. The Jaguars lost a tough, high-profile road game between division leaders Sunday â ending a three-game winning streak and sending the AFC South leaders into their first home game in nearly a month with a clear objective: Overcome adversity once again. "A lot of this for us is going to be about just settling back down," Head Coach Liam Coen said Monday, a day after the Jaguarsâ 23-18 loss to the NFC East-leading New York Giants at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J. Coen added that this week will be about, "Regathering, coming back with our play style, getting back to being physical in all three phases." The Jaguars typically have responded well to adversity under Coen, with a 5-1 record following losses in his two seasons as head coach. The Jaguars (7-3) this season beat the New England Patriots, 35-6, at home in Week 3 after a 20-13 road loss to the Denver Broncos in Week 2. After a 34-31 loss to the Houston Texans in London in Week 6, the Jaguars returned to Jacksonville after the bye week and beat the Indianapolis Colts, 42-7. "We got outplayed and outcoached in all three phases," Coen said. "When that occurs, you go back to basics. You go back to fundamentals, you go back to the simplicity of things to allow the players to go play freely, to go be able to communicate everything that they're seeing, and so much of that goes back to keep it simple and let the guys go play." The Jaguars were penalized 13 times for 107 yards with the Giants penalized six times for 46 yards.

JACKSONVILLE â The Jaguars play on the road again Sunday â this time with some new faces. The AFC South-leading Jaguars (7-2) will play the NFC East-leading New York Giants (5-3-1) at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J. , Sunday. Offensive Coordinator Grant Udinski and Defensive Coordinator Anthony Campanile spoke to the media Thursday at the Miller Electric Center and discuss â among other topics â the upcoming Jaguars debuts of defensive tackle Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III . A look at Thursday around the Jaguars: 1.Bates III and Davis are expected to play for the Jaguars for the first time Sunday, with the team giving the veteran defenders a "bye week" last week after acquiring them on the Monday before November 10 NFL trade deadline. "They've done all the work, so I am fired up about those guys," Campanile said Thursday. The Jaguars acquired Bates, a three-time All-Pro selection, from the Atlanta Falcons. They acquired Davis, a premier defensive tackle with All-Pro ability, from the Philadelphia Eagles with the moves coming the same day the Jaguars acquired nose tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints. The trio has drawn praise from coaches regarding their fit with the organization and work ethic, with Head Coach Liam Coen this week noting that Bates was in the "coaches' offices watching tape Saturday night before the game until about 11 o'clock and working through calls, going through pictures, going through as much communication as possible." Bates said such an approach is about doing "what I love." "It doesn't feel like we're cramming in stuff," Bates said.

items.summary: If the Raiders tight end can play this Sunday, he'll have a tough task ahead across the line of the scrimmage.
items.impact: Noted. No automatic usage shift from this item.
items.body: Key Matchups: Raiders hopeful for Brock Bowers' return in Sunday night showdown Nov 26, 2026 at 03:45 PM Levi Edwards Digital Team Reporter Copied! The Raiders will be under the bright lights Sunday night, when a national audience will tune in to see them face off against the Cleveland Browns. But with the spotlight comes added pressure. The Raiders will be on the road facing their fourth consecutive opponent with a winning record. As the Browns (6-4) continue their push toward playoff contention, the Raiders (4-7) face no easy road ahead in their effort to end a three-game skid. Here's a look at matchups on the offensive and defensive side of the ball to keep in mind for Sunday Night Football. Related Links Raiders Mailbag: Cornerback spot remains unsettled heading into matchup with Browns Game Preview: Raiders hit the road again for primetime test against Browns Gutierrez: Hope abounds with Fernando Mendoza in his second start Brock "Buddy" Bowers vs. Denzel Ward Browns coach Todd Monken has an immense amount of respect for Brock Bowers dating back to coaching the Raiders tight end in college at Georgia. As Bulldogs, they won back-to-back national championships in 2021 and 2022, and Bowers won his first of two John Mackey Awards in the latter season. Monken revealed this week that Bowers was affectionately given the nickname "Buddy the Yellow Lab" in college because he "could play ball all day and his tongue would be hanging out, and he never wanted to come out." "All he knows is one speed and work," Monken said of Bowers. "He gets that from mom and dad, who were Division I athletes, and he's wired the right way.
